name: Briscola Scoperta
description: Briscola Scoperta is an open-hand two-player variant of the Italian trick-taking game Briscola. Each player’s three-card hand and the top stock card are face up, and play uses the usual Briscola trump and point values while the buried stock cards remain unknown.

overview.description: Briscola Scoperta is an open-hand two-player variant of the Italian trick-taking game Briscola. Each player’s three-card hand and the top stock card are face up, and play uses the usual Briscola trump and point values while the buried stock cards remain unknown.

history.origins: Briscola Scoperta is an open-hand two-player variant of the Italian trick-taking game Briscola. It grew out of Italy's Ace-Ten trump-game tradition and keeps the same card values and scoring structure as standard Briscola.
timeline: 1600s–1700s: Briscola-type Ace-Ten games spread across Italy and become a staple of local card play.
Modern Era: Briscola Scoperta is documented as an open-hand variant of two-player Briscola for practice and analysis.

scoring.description: Card points won in tricks using the Briscola scale (A=11, 3=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2; others 0).
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach 61 or more card points from tricks wins the deal; a 60‑60 split is treated as a drawn game or redeal by agreement.

synthesis.shortDescription: Briscola Scoperta is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.
